claim: The spec's load-bearing architectural claim is "reuse the proven path, do not fork it" — that `budget check` "already sums Σ closed spans + open span correctly and is covered by resume tests" and that economics merely "imports and calls the *same* pure helpers." That is true only for the **top-line scalar**. The `--by model` / `--by class` fold is **new** logic that `budget check` never had to write: `budget check` reports a scalar `spent.tokens` and has no `--by model`/`--by class` axis (those are `economics`'s FAFF-410 surface). So the spec is not reusing a proven per-axis fold — it is authoring one, and then asserting it reconciles to the new top-line. The reconcile guarantee therefore depends on an identity the spec never establishes: that the open-span per-model base rows (built from the single-session transcript walk) sum to exactly `max(0, openSessionTotal − openBaseline)` **per the same clamp the top-line uses**. If the walk's per-model rows are derived from the raw whole-session totals and the top-line clamp is applied only to the scalar (or applied per-model with a different baseline shape), the model/class rows will sum to `openSessionTotal + closedSpend.total` rather than `max(0, openSessionTotal − openBaseline) + closedSpend.total`, and the "reconcile to `tokens_total`" promise — which the spec itself calls "load-bearing" and which §6 says it is *revising the docs to keep true* — breaks on exactly the resumed runs this ticket targets. The spec's own disjointness argument (§4) only proves the fold does not *double-count* the open walk; it says nothing about whether the open walk's per-model rows already reflect the rebaselined clamp.
evidence: §1 "Reuse the proven path, do not fork it" ("`budget check` already sums Σ closed spans + open span correctly and is covered by resume tests"); §3 "`--by class` / `--by model` reconciliation" ("Only these two axes fold"); §4 "Both the `model` and `class` folds sum, in tokens, to the same closed-span contribution added to the top-line, so both axes reconcile to `tokens_total` after the fold (the reconcile test asserts each)"; §6 "the reconcile sentence … is now false for `day` on a resumed run … revise it to say `class`/`model` always reconcile."
predicted_consequence: On a resumed run where the open span's `baseline_by_model_class` is non-zero (the spec's own §5 non-zero-baseline holdout), the `--by model`/`--by class` rows sum to more than `tokens_total` by exactly the open-span baseline that the top-line clamps away — the reconcile test the spec mandates ("rows sum to EXACTLY `tokens_total`, never more") fails, or the build agent is forced to invent a per-model clamp the spec never specified, forking the open-span methodology the spec forbids.

claim: §3/§4 say the `class` axis projects `closedSpend.byModel` onto classes by "add (Σ over models: closedSpend.byModel[model][c]) into the row keyed by class `c`, priced per model×class before summing." But `closedSpend.byModel` is a **token** map (per the §3 helper signature: `byModel: Map<model, {input,output,…}>`), and the `class` axis rows are keyed by class with no model dimension. "Priced per model×class before summing" requires the fold to retain a per-model price for each class contribution and then sum the *costs* — yet the axis row is a single class row. The spec never states whether the class row carries a cost column, how a multi-model class row aggregates per-model prices into one cost figure, or whether the token-sum and the cost-sum are both stored. If the fold sums tokens into the class row but prices the row at a single (open-span) model rate, the class-axis **cost** will not reconcile to `cost_total` on a map-priced resumed run even though its tokens do — and the spec's reconcile test only asserts the token sum ("rows sum (in tokens) to the top-line tokens_total"), so the cost-side drift is untested and uncaught.
evidence: §3 "The `class` axis … add (Σ over models: closedSpend.byModel[model][c]) into the row keyed by class `c`, priced per model×class before summing, so map-priced runs stay correct"; §5 holdout "the --by class rows sum (in tokens) to the top-line tokens_total (== 600)."
predicted_consequence: On a map-priced resumed run, `--by class` token rows reconcile but the class-axis cost does not reconcile to `cost_total`, and no test the spec defines catches it — the "map-priced runs stay correct" claim is asserted, not established.

claim: The fix routes the operator-supplied `--session-id` flag and the ambient `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` into `effectiveEnv` and then into `sessionOwnedTranscriptFiles(base, sid, runStartMs)`, which admits `${sid}.jsonl` (plus `agent-*.jsonl` children) as the files to read. The spec's only stated gate on that selection is the attribution check `childOwningSession(f) === sid` applied to the *children* — it never states that `sid` itself is validated or that the resolved path is confined to the run's transcript directory. A session id carrying path-traversal (`../../…`) or an absolute component would let the walk read a transcript file outside the intended run dir. This is a *new* input surface for `economics`: today it meters a single ambient session via the weak `economics.js:1075` line; the change adopts the FAFF-560 precedence that elevates the `--session-id` flag to highest precedence, so the flag value now directly selects the file the tool reads.
evidence: §3 WHAT — "effectiveEnv via SESSION PRECEDENCE … `measureSessionId = sessionIdFlag || openSpanSid || …`"; §4 HOW — "the single-session walk … selects files through `sessionOwnedTranscriptFiles(base, sid, runStartMs)` … which admits exactly `${sid}.jsonl` plus the `agent-*.jsonl` children gated by the attribution check `childOwningSession(f) === sid`"; §4 edge case — "`--session-id` flag supplied. Highest precedence — overrides the open-span session".
predicted_consequence: A crafted `--session-id` (or ambient `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`) resolves to a transcript path outside the run directory, so `faff economics` reads and folds an attacker-chosen file's token deltas into the reported run total — a path-traversal read that the spec's disjointness/reconcile reasoning does not bound, because it only proves disjointness *within* the admitted set, not that the admitted set stays inside the run dir.

claim: The new provenance warning interpolates ledger data into operator-facing output: "close_source != transcript: <list>" where the list is `degradedSpans` = `session_id ?? close_source` of each folded span. These values come from `run-ledger.json` (a persisted, third-party-writable artifact) and are emitted verbatim into the warning string with no stated escaping or length bound. If a span's `session_id`/`close_source` carries control characters or ANSI/terminal sequences, the warning becomes a log/terminal-injection vector in the very reporting surface this ticket adds.
evidence: §3 WHAT — `degradedSpans = … .map(s => s.session_id ?? s.close_source)`; §3 warning — `push "resumed run: N folded prior-epoch span(s) were measured with a degraded basis (close_source != transcript: <list>); …"`; §8 DONE — "A folded span with `close_source != "transcript"` surfaces a provenance warning, threaded via `degraded_close_sources`".
predicted_consequence: A ledger span whose `session_id`/`close_source` embeds escape sequences or newlines is reflected unescaped into the economics warning, enabling log/terminal injection in the report output.

claim: The DONE item "Map-pricing per-model delta folds `closedSpend.byModel` … so `cost_total` spans epochs" is not decided by any scenario. Every `--by model` / `--by class` holdout asserts that the rows sum **in tokens** to `tokens_total` (== 600); none asserts that the emitted `cost_total` (or the per-row cost) includes the closed-span contribution. A build that folds the closed-span token counts into the per-model delta but prices only the open-span portion (or prices the pre-fold delta and appends the closed tokens unpriced) passes every token-reconcile scenario while shipping a `cost_total` that is still epoch-scoped — the exact defect the ticket exists to close, on the cost axis.
evidence: DONE "Map-pricing per-model delta folds `closedSpend.byModel` (mirror `budget.js:1052-1058`) so `cost_total` spans epochs"; holdout scenarios `--by model` / `--by class` both assert "rows sum (in tokens) to the top-line tokens_total (== 600)" only; the main scenario asserts `tokens_total == 600` and `tokens_source == "transcript"` only.
predicted_consequence: done cannot be decided for the cost axis: a build with a correct `tokens_total` (600) and a `cost_total` equal to the open-epoch cost only (e.g. pricing 100 tokens, not 600) satisfies every named scenario and every other DONE item, yet the "cost-per-shipped-issue" headline — the surface this ticket is about — still under-reports a resumed run.

claim: The DONE item "`--by day|mcp|effort|phase` do NOT fold and emit a coverage warning naming them as resuming-epoch-only on a resumed run" names four axes; the only scenario exercises `--by day`. `mcp`, `effort`, and `phase` have no scenario, so a build that emits the warning for `day` but not for the other three (or folds one of them) cannot be caught by the named acceptance set.
evidence: DONE "`--by day|mcp|effort|phase` do NOT fold and emit a coverage warning…"; holdout scenario "Given the resumed 2-epoch ledger → When `faff economics --by day` → a warning names the per-day breakdown as covering the resuming epoch only" — `day` only.
predicted_consequence: done cannot be decided for `--by mcp`, `--by effort`, `--by phase`: a build that warns on `day` but silently omits the warning (or silently folds) on the other three axes passes every named scenario.
